frequency_question: How often do Treasury-announced secondary sanctions against major foreign banks cleanly match the written formal criteria without technical loopholes or watered-down waivers?
membership_rule: Includes formal OFAC designations or correspondent banking bans on top-tier foreign commercial banks for sanctions evasion; excludes informal warnings, diplomatic reprimands, or penalties settled solely via minor consent decrees without loss of U.S. financial system access.

cases.name: Bank of Kunlun (China) - secondary sanctions under NDAA
Commercial Bank of Iraq - secondary sanctions for Iran/IRGC

provenance_note: 3 cases named, 4 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.3x)
coverage_note: 3 named; believed roughly 4 in total meeting the exact major bank secondary sanctions threshold since 2010.
known_gaps: Excludes minor non-bank entities and general advisories not reaching the level of cutting off access to the U.S. financial system.
skeleton: Total major foreign bank secondary sanction actions with explicit U.S. financial system cutoffs vs. total threatened or partially implemented actions involving waivers or delayed enforcement.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 4 total formal major actions where written criteria were fully invoked without administrative backing down.
validity_reason: Statutory frameworks for secondary sanctions (like CAATSA and NDAA authorities) remain stable across administrations, ensuring consistent drafting patterns.
